title: Video Understanding: Sample Time Before Modeling It

questions.question: What extra structure must a video pipeline preserve compared with a single image?
options: The temporal order and sampling relationship between frames
A second RGB color space for every frame
Only the largest frame's spatial resolution
A random label for each timestamp
questions.explanation: Video adds a time axis. Sampling, pooling, and splitting must preserve or intentionally summarize that order.

questions.question: What does `sample_uniform(10,4)` return in this lesson?
questions.explanation: The implementation floors i*10/4 for i=0..3, producing 0, 2, 5, and 7, all valid frame indices.

questions.question: What property distinguishes `sample_dense(20,5,seeded_rng)` from uniform sampling?
options: It returns one contiguous five-frame clip with a reproducible start
It always returns the first five frames
It samples five different videos
It can return an index equal to 20
questions.explanation: When enough frames exist, dense sampling selects start..start+T-1. The seeded generator makes the start reproducible and all indices stay below 20.

questions.question: Why does `inflate_kernel_2d` divide repeated temporal slices by `time_kernel`?
options: So summing the new temporal slices recovers the original spatial kernel
To change the number of input channels
To make every temporal slice zero
So the kernel can ignore the frame axis
questions.explanation: Repeating the 2D weights and dividing by the number of copies preserves their temporal average and keeps the original spatial response as the time sum.

questions.question: For `temporal_split(10,0.6)`, which boundary is returned?
options: Training 0..5 and test 6..9
Training 0..4 and test 5..9
Training every even frame and test every odd frame
The same frame indices in both sets
questions.explanation: floor(10*0.6)=6, so the half-open training range is 0..5 and the test range starts at 6.

questions.question: Which architecture choice fits a task that only needs an order-insensitive average of frame features?
options: Temporal pooling after a frame encoder
A larger spatial kernel with no time axis
A random frame split that duplicates future clips
A detector box without any temporal aggregation
questions.explanation: `temporal_pool` explicitly averages selected frame features. A temporal convolution or attention block is needed only when local or long-range order matters.
